 Kentucky Basketball is winning, but the margin may be hurting some of you
 Kentucky has failed to cover the spread in every game this season, a sharp drop from Mark Pope’s average betting record.
 by dholbrook Nov 17, 2026, 11:05 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 Dylan Ballard - A Sea Of Blue Kentucky Basketball has won games by 28, 9, and 29 points, and lost by 20. Do you know what they haven’t done? Covered a single spread all year long.
 That fact will not matter to the fans who only care about the win-loss column, but to some of you out there, and you know exactly who you are, it matters a lot.
 Point spreads are the clearest indicator of expectations, and right now, the Wildcats are falling short of those expectations that Vegas has set. The latest came Monday night when Kentucky was a 30-point favorite over Grambling State, but a late bucket by the Tigers in the closing seconds led to the Cats winning by just 29.
 The Cats are currently one of just 11 college basketball programs to fail to cover the spread in any of their opening four+ games. The oddsmakers are setting a bar, and Kentucky is not able to hit it.
 That could be good if you are betting against the Cats.
 Mark Pope has been okay ATS at Kentucky
 When you look back at Mark Pope’s squad last season, they finished exactly 18-18 against the spread. Breaking down the national betting data from across the country, that flat 50 percent cover rate is the exact median of college basketball, per TeamRankings. 
 Last year, Kentucky sat dead in the middle of the road alongside programs like Virginia, Texas Tech, UNLV, and Rutgers. Vegas had Pope’s team pegged perfectly. They were no better or worse than the numbers suggested.
 But this year is a different story.
 Winning the buy games is the ultimate goal, and Kentucky has done that so far. But it is interesting to see how Vegas views the Cats versus how they perform on the court.
